internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The status of being the preferred/superior good: that which is (or would be) singled out over alternatives as the more choiceworthy/beneficial option; and, in the verbal derivations, the act of singling that preferred thing out (to choose/select). Residue = PREFERENCE-OF-THE-GOOD (choiceworthiness).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every kh-y-r word in the set turns on one axis: that which is preferred because it is good (the better, the best, the choiceworthy), and in the verbs the act of singling that out. The comparative khayrun-min ("better than": 38:76 Iblis "I am better than him", 97:3 "better than a thousand months", 2:221, 27:36) names X as the preferred term of a comparison. The construct khayru + genitive-plural ("best of judges/providers/creation": 10:109, 22:58, 98:7; 3:110 khayra ummatin "best community") names the topmost of a class. Bare khayr ("good/benefit/wealth": 100:8 love of khayr, 2:180 "if he leaves khayr", 2:215, 22:36 "in them is khayr for you", 70:21 "khayr touches him") names the desirable-good one loves, spends, is touched by. Khayrat ("good things/deeds": 2:148 and 5:48 "race to the khayrat", 21:90, 23:61, 9:88) names the choiceworthy things one competes for. The verbs (Form VIII ikhtara/ikhtartuka: 20:13, 44:32 "over the worlds", 7:155 "singled out as preferred"; Form V yatakhayyarun/takhayyarun: 56:20, 68:38 "pick what they prefer"; and al-khiyarah: 28:68, 33:36 "the prerogative of choice") enact that same preference as an act of selection. Across all 196 the root supplies the preferred-good; form, construction and context supply the comparison, superlative frame, referent or agency.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: the ADJ occurrences are comparative/elative; the grammar supplies the "-er/most" and the min-frame, the root only the axis of comparison (preferability). CONSTRUCTION: khayru + genitive-plural is the superlative "best of X" (the frame is construction; the root supplies "topmost/most-preferred of the class"); definite al-khayr / plural khayrat nominalize it as "the good / the good things." VERBAL DERIVATION: Form VIII/V supply "perform the act of," the root supplies "single out the preferred." PARTICIPANTS/CONTEXT supply the referent (God as chooser, wealth as the good, deeds as khayrat, the Hereafter as the better abode) and the valence. Subtracting all of these, the invariant residue is: being, or picking out, the preferred/choiceworthy good. Internal anchors confirm the axis is preference and not bare goodness: 2:61 contrasts khayr with adna (the lower/inferior), and khayr repeatedly pairs-yet-differs with ahsan (17:35, 4:59, 19:73, 25:24: "khayr wa-ahsan"), showing khayr carries the comparative/preferential load while ahsan carries intrinsic goodness.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: khayru al-makirin "best of schemers" (3:54, 8:30) and Iblis's ana khayrun minhu "I am better than him" (7:12, 38:76). In the first, the class (makr) is not itself morally good, yet the root still contributes "the pre-eminent/most-effective of the class" (superiority/preference), with the valence supplied by context, not the root. In the second, the claim is false, yet the root still contributes an asserted superiority/preferability; the falsehood is contextual, not a different root sense. Neither breaks universal presence: preference-of-the-superior remains the residue.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: That the core is simply GOOD / BENEFICIAL (positive moral or material value). This covers the nominal and adjectival occurrences smoothly but strains on the verbal branch: ikhtara "to choose" (20:13, 7:155), takhayyara "to pick/prefer" (56:20, 68:38) and al-khiyarah "the choice/prerogative" (28:68, 33:36) are about SELECTION, not goodness, and do not reduce to "good." The preferred hypothesis (preference-of-the-good / choiceworthiness) subsumes both the valuation branch (better/best/good) and the selection branch (choose/the-choice) under one axis, which "good" alone cannot.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from HSN (hasan, intrinsic goodness/beauty): khayr co-occurs with and is set beside ahsan (17:35, 4:59, 19:73, 25:24), so they are not identical; khayr carries the comparative/preferential axis, hasan the intrinsic-quality axis. Distinct from FDL (fadl, bestowed bounty/surplus-favor) and NF' (naf', benefit): khayr is specifically the preferred/superior option, anchored by the min-comparison and by the adna-contrast (2:61 "would you exchange what is khayr for what is adna"). The residue is non-empty (preference/choiceworthiness), falsifiable (a khayr-occurrence with no preferential/choiceworthy dimension would break it), and distinctive against the nearest roots.
unresolved_cases: Softest (present but least explicit): the 'wealth/property' nominal sense (2:180 in taraka khayran; 100:8 li-hubbi al-khayr; 38:32 hubba al-khayr) reads primarily as 'good/wealth', with the preference/choiceworthiness dimension present only implicitly (wealth as the desirable-sought-good). It is reconcilable but carries the interpretive load.
khayru al-makirin (3:54, 8:30): reconciled as 'pre-eminent of the class' with contextual valence; noted as the point where 'good' valence and 'preferred/superior' most visibly separate.
internal_discovery.rationale: Full coverage: all 196 confirmed occurrences assessed, and each reconciles to one non-empty residue: the preferred/choiceworthy good (and, verbally, its selection). No occurrence breaks presence. The synthesis is not imposed: internal evidence fixes the axis as PREFERENCE rather than bare goodness (the adna-contrast at 2:61; the recurring khayr-vs-ahsan pairing at 17:35/4:59/19:73/25:24; the min-comparative frame; and the verbal branch ikhtara/takhayyara/al-khiyarah which is selection, not goodness). The residue is distinctive against hasan/fadl/naf' and is falsifiable. Rated STRONG rather than MODERATE because presence is universal across a very large set with strong internal anchors; not maximal because unifying the pure 'good/wealth' nominals with the 'choose' verbals requires the interpretive bridge of 'choiceworthiness', and a handful of occurrences (wealth-sense; khayru al-makirin) carry that bridge's load rather than displaying preference overtly.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Full coverage read: 196/196 occurrences. The residue is deliberately double-barreled — a distinctive comparative/selective core ("singled out over alternatives as more choiceworthy" + verbal "choose/select") welded to a generic quality ("beneficial/good"). The core (a) holds cleanly and is distinctive wherever khayr sits in a comparison or is a choose-verb: elative frames with min/am (e.g. 12:39, 16:30, 27:36, 97:3, 43:52, 3:157), superlative construct khayru l-... (khayr al-hakimin 10:109, al-raziqin 23:72, al-ghafirin 7:155, al-makirin 3:54/8:30, al-fasilin 6:57, al-fatihin 7:89, khayr al-bariyya 98:7, khayr umma 3:110), and the verbal derivations (ikhtara VIII 20:13, 44:32, 7:155; takhayyara V 56:20, 68:38; al-khiyara 28:68, 33:36). For that structured subset (~half the tokens) the verdict would be SUPPORTED.

REFUTATION of UNIVERSAL PRESENCE: a large nominal class uses khayr as a substance/polar category where NO comparison and NO act of choosing is present, so the distinctive "preference / singled-out-over-alternatives / choiceworthiness" element is not demonstrable — only bare "good/beneficial" survives. Sharpest failures: khayr = concrete wealth/property — 100:8 (hubb al-khayr = love of wealth), 2:180 (in taraka khayran = leaves property for bequest), 38:32 (Solomon's hubb al-khayr = fine horses/wealth), 2:215, 2:272, 2:273 (ma anfaqtum/tunfiqu min khayr = wealth spent), 33:25 (lam yanalu khayran = gained no benefit), 33:19 (ashihhatan 'ala l-khayr = greedy for wealth), 50:25 & 68:12 (mannaa' li-l-khayr = withholder of good/wealth), 7:188 (lastakthartu mina l-khayr), 3:26 (bi-yadika l-khayr); and khayr = the good-fortune POLE antonymous to sharr (a neutral test/affliction category, not a preferred option) — 21:35 (bi-sh-sharri wa-l-khayri fitnatan), 70:21 (massahu l-khayr), 22:11 (asabahu khayrun), 17:11 (du'aa'ahu bi-l-khayr), 41:49 (du'aa' al-khayr), 11:84 (arakum bi-khayr = in prosperity), 6:17 & 10:107 (yamsaska/yuridka bi-khayr), 28:24 (min khayr faqir). In every one of these the referent is a thing/state, not something singled out over alternatives; "choiceworthiness" is imputed, not evidenced.

DISTINCTIVENESS problem: the two readings trade off. To make the residue universal you must weaken it to "the good/beneficial," which is exactly the semantic space shared with husn (h-s-n), tayyib (T-y-b), fadl (f-D-l), ni'ma (n-E-m) — not distinctive. Keep it distinctive (preference/choice) and it demonstrably fails the ~21 flagged occurrences. Under non-negotiable root unity, unreconciled occurrences mean verdict != SUPPORTED. The contribution is real and dominant but not universally present as a single distinctive residue, hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (not REFUTED — the proposed sense is correct for a large structured subset).
